messages:
jess_customer: Hey team — our embeddings endpoint suddenly dropped vectors/sec by ~60% an hour ago, tokens/sec looks unchanged. Customers seeing timeouts. No recent deploys on our side.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that, Jess. Can you paste the last few request IDs and a sample request body? Are you getting any 4xx/5xx?

jess_customer: Request IDs: r-9f3a2c, r-9f3a2d, r-9f3a2f. No 5xx, just many requests taking 3–8s to return vs ~0.8s previously. No 4xx. Payload is standard embeddings array of short text.

alex_eng: Thanks — can you confirm model name + variant and if you changed batch settings? Also any sudden increase in batch size from client side?

jess_customer: model: openvec-large-v2, variant: default. We haven't changed client batching. Calls are individual (single input) at ~120 qps.

maria_support: Noted. We're triaging. Sam, can you check GPU queue depth / slot availability for the tenant region?

sam_prodops: Looking now. I see elevated queue depth on a small subset of pods since 10:12 UTC. GPU util per pod is normal (~55%) but waiters count is high. Kernel wait log shows multiple KV cache locks.

sre-bot: [alert] high_waiters detected cluster=eu-west-1 pool=vec-serving-2 threshold=20 current=47

alex_eng: KV cache lock spikes usually cause throughput to collapse for vectorized paths while token paths remain stable. Could be a prefix-cache eviction storm or a batch-dimension mismatch causing extra memcpy.

maria_support: @jess_customer can you share a raw curl example (sanitized) so we can repro locally?

jess_customer: Sure — here's a minimal repro: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"openvec-large-v2","input":["short text "],"client_batch":1}'

alex_eng: Trying this against staging. Quick check: any chance your client is sometimes sending arrays of vectors (pre-embedded) mixed with raw text? That can trigger dimension validation code paths and fallback conversion which is slower.

jess_customer: Nope, always raw text.

sam_prodops: I pulled svc logs for r-9f3a2c. I see repeated lines: 

[2026-02-12T10:13:02Z] WARN kvcache: lock-timeout key=prefix:abc duration=120ms waiters=12
[2026-02-12T10:13:02Z] DEBUG batcher: batch-window extended to 30ms due to backlog

alex_eng: That matches a batching expansion loop — batcher increases window because queue is deep which increases latency per request and decreases vectors/sec. Root cause could be a slow downstream op (KV lock, host IO).

maria_support: Any auth/billing anomalies? We've seen auth retries sometimes amplify load.

sre-bot: billing: no anomalies for tenant jess_corp; auth: token refresh spikes 0.2% around 10:10 (normal).

alex_eng: Two actionable things: 1) try pinning to a lighter model variant (openvec-large-v2-quant8) to see if kernel path eliminates memcpy overhead, 2) enable client-side small-batch aggregation (batching on client to 4) to reduce per-request overhead.

maria_support: Jess, can you temporarily reroute a small percentage (5–10%) of traffic to quant8 variant for testing? If throughput returns, we'll know KVM/kernel path is culprit.

jess_customer: Spun up a canary to quant8 for 10% now. Will report in ~2m.

[120s later]

jess_customer: Canary looks good — vectors/sec recovered ~2.8x for quant8. Default variant still slow on remaining 90%.

alex_eng: Good repro. That strongly implicates runtime kernel selection / memory path. Sam — can you capture a perf profile from an affected pod? Look for memcpy, cuda-synchronization spikes, and any futex/KV lock contention.

sam_prodops: Perf captured. Top lines: nio memcpy (host->device) increased by 3x, then futex wait in kvcache. Also saw an anomalous GC in a helper process around same time (collector pause ~200ms every 2s).

maria_support: Collector pause could hold a lock causing those kvcache waiters. Any recent agent/sidecar rollout?

sam_prodops: There was a metrics-sidecar rollout at 09:58 UTC to v2.4.7 — changelog mentions new histogram aggregator. Rolling back now on affected pool.

sre-bot: [deploy] rollback initiated service=metrics-sidecar pool=vec-serving-2 user=sam_prodops

alex_eng: If rollback removes GC pauses, that should reduce lock hold times and restore vectors/sec. Meanwhile recommend client mitigation: aggregate inputs into batches of 4 and switch 10–20% to quant8.

maria_support: Jess, sorry for the disruption. We'll monitor until rollback completes and will update. Also filing a postmortem runbook item to detect metric-sidecar GC impacts on kvcache locks.

[rollback completes]

sam_prodops: Rollback finished at 10:30 UTC. Queue depth dropping, waiters back to normal.

jess_customer: Confirming — vectors/sec back to baseline and latency restored to ~0.9s. Thank you all.

maria_support: Closing loop: root cause = metrics-sidecar v2.4.7 GC behavior indirectly holding kvcache locks causing memcpy/backpressure and expanded batch windows. Mitigation = rollback and client-side batching + optional model-variant pin while we harden.

alex_eng: Follow-ups: (1) add detection rule for long-lived collector pauses correlated with kvcache locks, (2) evaluate sidecar memory tuning or replace histogram aggregator, (3) publish recommended client batch size guidance.

jess_customer: Appreciated. Please share any changelog/monitoring alerts we should watch.

maria_support: Will DM you alert links and a short summary. :white_check_mark: 

sre-bot: [incident] resolved incident_id=INC-2026-0212-veclock-01 duration=18m
